defs.example: Traffic is slow at rush hour.

defs.text: Traffic is the buying and selling of goods, especially illegal goods.
defs.example: Governments are working to prevent the abduction and sale of, or traffic in children.

defs.text: a visual signal to control the flow of traffic at intersections
Courage is the quality of not being afraid easily.
defs.example: The warrior had great courage.

defs.text: A hunt is a search for something or someone.
defs.example: The police were on a hunt to find the murderer.

defs.text: A hunt is a search for animal(s) to catch or kill.
If you hunt for something, you look for it very carefully.
defs.example: We hunted for new clothing at the mall.

defs.text: If you hunt for animals, you look for them to catch or kill them.
defs.example: My father hunted rabbits when I was a child.

defs.text: Rats are medium-sized rodents. They often live near people and eat garbage. Rats can carry diseases. They are also kept as pets and can be very tame.
defs.example: I caught the rat that was eating our food.

defs.text: If a person, animal, or plant is ill, it has a disease.
defs.example: 1.4 million children suffer from heart disease in Pakistan.

defs.text: A winner is someone that has won a competition, or often wins.
defs.example: Terry is considered the winner since he came in first in the 100 meters race event.

defs.text: A council is a group of people who are chosen or elected to make laws, rules, and decisions.
defs.example: Town council is considering a road-widening proposal.

defs.text: An appointment is a formal agreement to meet or visit someone (for example, a doctor) at a certain time and place.
defs.example: I have a doctor's appointment at 3:00 tomorrow.

defs.text: The second day of the week. The first day of the work week.
defs.example: I hate Mondays.

defs.text: A crack is the line where something is breaking.
defs.example: There is a crack from the edge of this plate to the middle. It will break soon.

defs.text: A loud sound like the sound of something breaking.
defs.example: It was raining, and she saw a flash of lightning and heard the crack of thunder.

defs.text: A strong, fairly cheap form of cocaine; crack often comes in the form of a rock and it is usually smoked in a crack-pipe.
defs.example: "I wouldn't use it, if I was going to use it I can afford real cocaine. Crack is wack." - Whitney Houston

defs.text: When something cracks it breaks along a line, maybe not a straight line. It might break into two pieces, or it might break but the two pieces are still attached.
defs.example: She cracked an egg and put the inside of the egg into a bowl.

defs.text: A threat is something or someone that might be bad or dangerous, or cause a problem.
defs.example: The product posed a serious health threat and should not be used.

defs.text: A threat is the words somebody uses to tell you they will do something bad to you unless you do what they want you to.
defs.example: He made a lot of threats, but he didn't do anything.

defs.text: A physical thing or activity is related to the body, or something you can touch.
defs.example: The war didn't leave him with any physical injuries, but his mind was badly damaged.

defs.text: A nation is a country or a political entity.
defs.example: Mexico is a nation of emigrants.

defs.text: The source of some material, an idea, a product, etc. is the place it came from originally.
defs.example: XYZ company can't supply these parts anymore, so we need to find a new source.

defs.text: A healthy person is someone who is not sick. They are strong and will probably live a long time.
defs.example: I need three young, healthy people to help me.

defs.text: Healthy things leads to better health.
defs.example: Healthy food is full of vitamins and minerals.

defs.text: A victory is the act or result of winning.
defs.example: The Korean War had no clear victory.

defs.text: If something is disgusting, it causes someone to have a strong dislike for it.
A palace is the home of a king or queen.
defs.example: Elizabeth II of England lives in a palace in London, called Buckingham Palace.

defs.text: A palace is a big, very grand house, often the home of someone important like a president or bishop.
defs.example: During the revolution, soldiers guarded the gates of the president's palace.

defs.text: searching for or buying goods or services
defs.example: went shopping for a reliable plumber

defs.text: the commodities purchased from stores
defs.example: she loaded her shopping into the car"women carrying home shopping didn't give me a second glance

defs.text: A neighborhood is part of a town or city.
defs.example: They live in an Italian neighborhood on the west side of the city.

defs.text: Somebody or something's neighborhood is the area, people, or ideas around or near them.
defs.example: He goes to church on Sundays and has lunch at a restaurant in his neighborhood.

defs.text: The third (3rd) month in the year.
defs.example: There are 31 days in March.

defs.text: A formal, rhythmic way of walking. A march is usually done by soldiers, bands and in .
A political rally or parade.
Any song in the genre of music written for marching (see Wikipedia's article on this type of music)
To walk with long, regular strides, like a soldier does.
defs.example: We saw the guards marching at Buckingham Palace.

defs.text: To go to war; to make military advances.
12:00 am; the middle of the night.
An advantage is a condition or circumstance that favors success.
An advantage is when someone has superiority over someone else.
An advantage is a benefit, gain, or profit.
If something is pure, it is not dirty or covered by anything that makes it unclean.
on or to one side
defs.example: step aside

defs.text: out of the way (especially away from one's thoughts)
defs.example: brush the objections aside

defs.text: not taken into account or excluded from consideration
defs.example: these problems apart, the country is doing well

defs.text: Mail is the messages and packages that you send to other people.
defs.example: There's no mail today because the post office is closed.

defs.text: If you mail something, you send it through the post.
defs.example: I mailed a birthday card to him last week.

defs.text: Half-light in the sky before sunrise.
defs.example: He woke up before dawn to do a morning jog.

defs.text: An effect is something that is caused by something else.
defs.example: His comments had a visible effect on those who heard it.

defs.text: If a law, agreement, change, etc. takes effect, it officially begins.
defs.example: The closing of the company takes effect at midnight.

defs.text: A sound effect is a way to make a sound for a performance artificially.
defs.example: The used a lot of normal materials to create the sound effects for the show.

defs.text: A special effect is a way to make an image for a performance artificially.
defs.example: They didn't really cut his hand off, but the special effect made it look real.

defs.text: A spell is an amount of time.
defs.example: He stayed in his house for quite a spell.

defs.text: What happens during an amount of time.
defs.example: We've had a bad spell of weather.

defs.text: Words supposed to have a magical power, or the effect they are supposed to have.
defs.example: He cast a spell on us.

defs.text: To make up a word.
defs.example: C, A and T spell cat.

defs.text: To say or write all the letters that make up a word, in the right order.
defs.example: Jack says: "Spell cat for me, Jill."

defs.text: To spell all the words in a language correctly.
defs.example: Jack says: I thought cat was spelled K-A-T.

defs.text: 01 + 02 00 | lose one's nerve
defs.example: When he saw the accident, he freaked out

defs.text: Wood is what trees are made of. People use wood to build things like houses and furniture.
If you are awake, you are not asleep.
defs.example: It was 1:00 AM and Gerard was still awake.

defs.text: A vacation is some time, usually between a week and a month, when people do not have to go to work, but get paid.
defs.example: Our last vacation was very nice.

defs.text: Violence is an action done to hurt somebody or something.
defs.example: I don't watch boxing, because I don't like all the fighting and violence.

defs.text: Someone's grandmother is the mother of one of their parents.
defs.example: The mother of my mother is Jane Smith. Jane Smith is my grandmother.

defs.text: If something is modern, it happened in current times.
defs.example: The new house has all modern conveniences.

defs.text: Some new styles or forms of art and fiction writing are called modern.
defs.example: Much modern art looks odd to many people.

defs.text: A firm object is hard and solid.
A firm is a group of people who work together as a business.
defs.example: John & John is a law firm.

defs.text: A firm is a group of people that come together to make money.
01 + 01 00 | become taut or tauter
defs.example: Your muscles will firm when you exercise regularly

defs.text: 02 + 08 00 + 11 00 | make taut or tauter
defs.example: tauten a rope

defs.text: If something is prime, it is best, most important, most suitable, or in some way number one.
defs.example: Canada is a prime example of a multicultural country.

defs.text: A prime minister is the head of government in a Westminster-style democracy.
defs.example: The Prime Minister is the leader of England.

defs.text: When talking about a specific prime minister, prime minister is capitalized.
defs.example: The Prime Minister gave a speech today.

defs.text: When calling a prime minister by their title and name together, British usage is the Prime Minister, Rishi Sunak or Rishi Sunak, the Prime Minister. North American usage is Prime Minister Rishi Sunak.
If you have a talent in doing something, you have the skill and ability to do that task.
defs.example: He has got the talent in music, but his family is too poor to provide him with the proper education.

defs.text: A piano is a large musical instrument that has hammers connected to 88 keys.
The act of giving a formal (usually written) authorization.
defs.example: It was decided to license Wikipedia under the GFDL.

defs.text: Officially authorize.
defs.example: I am licensed to practice law in this state.

defs.text: the act of preparing something (as food) by the application of heat
defs.example: cooking can be a great art

defs.text: A concern about something means something that a person is worried about.
defs.example: The government expressed its concern at the fighting in Kenya.

defs.text: A concern with something means something that a person is interested in or involved with.
Concern is a feeling that a person wants to help someone.
defs.example: Her look of concern made him feel better.

defs.text: A concern is a business.
defs.example: XYZ Company is an ongoing concern, and we have no plans to shut it down.

defs.text: If x concerns y, x is about y.
defs.example: We have received a letter that concerns the recent sale of the property.

defs.text: If something concerns a person, they think it is a problem or needs attention.
defs.example: The recent losses certainly concern me, but I still think things are looking good.

defs.text: You use to whom it may concern at the beginning of a letter when you don't know the name of the person you're writing to.
If something is available, it exists and you can use it.
defs.example: We can't answer the question with the available information.

defs.text: A factory is a building where lots of things are made.
defs.example: This factory makes one hundred cars every day.

defs.text: A factory is anything that makes other things, especially if it makes a really large amount of things.
Something's value is how good or important it is; how much money someone will exchange a thing for; an amount of money.
defs.example: The value for me of this food is $100.

defs.text: Your values are your ideas about which things are good.
defs.example: He has strong values.

defs.text: If you value someone or something, you think that they are good and you don't want to lose them.
defs.example: I value your help.

defs.text: If you value something judge how good or important it is.
defs.example: They valued it at $600.

defs.text: A thing is central when it is in the middle.
defs.example: The house is central to all of the stores.

defs.text: A union is when many things are joined together.
defs.example: The League of Nations was a union between many nations.

defs.text: A union may be the act of joining.
defs.example: The union of these two companies was painless.

defs.text: A very reflective surface which light can bounce off of.
defs.example: She kept staring at the mirror all day.

defs.text: A studio is a place where an artist makes art
A studio is a place where art or music is taught
A studio is a place where radio or television shows, records or films are made.
The radio show Music and Musings was broadcast from the studios of KOXY
The (mass) media is/are the news sources and the people behind them.
defs.example: The media have been too accepting of the government's arguments.

defs.text: A medium is a way of information or art.
defs.example: We have to use music, pictures and other media to sell the product.

defs.text: A taxi is a vehicle (usually a car) driven by a taxi driver; the taxi driver drives you somewhere if you pay them money.
An element with the symbol Fe and the atomic number 26.
defs.example: A way to melt iron at very high temperatures to make steel was developed in Sri Lanka in 300 BC.

defs.text: A metal from the element.
defs.example: That door is made of iron.

defs.text: A tool which uses heat to remove wrinkles from cloth.
defs.example: She used the iron on her skirt.

defs.text: To remove wrinkles with an iron.
defs.example: He irons his shirts.

defs.text: A wish, a feeling of want.
defs.example: She has a desire to win.

defs.text: A thing that someone wants.
defs.example: Love is my desire.

defs.text: To wish for something, to want something.
defs.example: I desire your company.

defs.text: If you rob something or someone, you steal from them.
defs.example: He went to rob the bank.

defs.text: A monkey is a primate with a long tail that climbs trees.
defs.example: We saw Vervet monkeys in the Zoo.

defs.text: Pride is the state of being proud.
A pride is a group of lions.
A miracle is an amazing thing that happened that seemed very unlikely to happen.
defs.example: Thanks to a miracle, Jane recovered from the final stage of cancer.

defs.text: A swim is when someone swims.
defs.example: We all went for a swim in the lake.

defs.text: If you swim, you move through the water using your arms and legs.
defs.example: Let's go swimming at the beach.

defs.text: If you are Christian then you are a Christian. (See noun above.)
defs.example: Yes, she is Christian.

defs.text: If something is Christian, it has to do with Christianity.
defs.example: Being saved from sin by Christ is a Christian idea.

defs.text: If something you do is Christian it something Christians are supposed to do.
defs.example: The way you forgave them was very Christian.

defs.text: A hook is a curved, sharp thing, usually made of metal and often small. Someone can put the hook through a hole in something to grip it so that they can pull the thing.
If you are hooking something, you are attaching it to a hook.
defs.example: Hook the bag here, and the conveyor will carry it away.

defs.text: Protection is keeping something or someone safe.
defs.example: She ran away from her abusive husband to her brother for protection.

defs.text: A device used for safe sex e.g. condom.
defs.example: I used protection so I wouldn't get her pregnant.

defs.text: A treatment is an action, usually by a doctor, to make somebody healthy.
defs.example: He has had treatments every day since he hurt his neck.

defs.text: The treatment that you give someone or something is the way that you act toward it.
defs.example: The treatment that I have received since beginning this job has been terrible. My boss yells at me every day and nobody is friendly at all.

defs.text: A part of the head (or face) used for hearing.
defs.example: My rabbit has two big ears.

defs.text: Metal is a hard material, often shiny and easy to conduct electricity. Gold, silver, and steel are examples of metals.
defs.example: We replaced out our wood door with a stronger metal one.

defs.text: If something disappears, it becomes impossible to see.
defs.example: For a moment the tiny redness of his cigarette was visible; then he disappeared into the darkness.

defs.text: If something disappears, it doesn't exist anymore.
defs.example: I can't say that my negative attitude toward life has entirely disappeared.

defs.text: If something has disappeared, you can't find it.
defs.example: Have you seen my keys? They've disappeared again.

defs.text: If you are grateful for or about something, you want to say, "thank you" because of it.
defs.example: I'm very grateful for your kindness during this difficult time.

defs.text: Extremely means to a very high degree.
defs.example: It is extremely difficult to climb Mount Everest without oxygen tanks.

defs.text: Treasure is a collection of valuable things, such as gold, diamonds, money, etc.
defs.example: Going after buried treasure is just as scary in real life as it is in the movies.

defs.text: A treasure is something or someone that is very valuable or important.
defs.example: As an actor, he's a national treasure.

defs.text: A rescue is a saving of someone or something.
defs.example: We saw his rescue from the burning house.

defs.text: A rescue is a freeing of someone or something.
defs.example: The soldiers rescue of their target from the prison was all they could talk about.

defs.text: If you rescue someone, you save them from any violence, emergency, or evil.
defs.example: The lifeguard jumped into the swimming pool to rescue the drowning woman.

defs.text: If you rescue someone, you free them from a prison or some other physical restraint.
defs.example: After capturing the enemy army, they rescued the prisoners.

defs.text: If you rescue something, you take it back using force.
If someone or something is capable of something, they can do it.
defs.example: This system is capable of providing food for about 400 people.

defs.text: If someone is capable, they can do a particular thing well.
defs.example: I'm confident I can leave everything in your capable hands.

defs.text: The solution of a mathematical equation.
defs.example: The result of 1 + 1 is 2.

defs.text: The situation at the end of a process, its outcome.
defs.example: The result of losing the presents was that everyone was sad.

defs.text: If x results in y, it leads to or causes y.
defs.example: A lot of digging results in a deep hole.

defs.text: If x results from y, it comes for or is caused by y.
defs.example: A deep hole resulted from all the digging.

defs.text: The sufferings of a person is the pain or distress they are going through.
A governor is a person who leads a place like a state or territory.
defs.example: The king appointed a new governor for the province.

defs.text: Text is written language (often academic).
defs.example: The text is OK, but we need to change the graphics before we publish.

defs.text: A text is a textbook (American English).
defs.example: Did you buy the text for the accounting course?

defs.text: A text is a message from a cell phone.
defs.example: I'll give you a text on your phone about tonight's concert.

defs.text: If you text someone, you send them a text message on their cell phone.
defs.example: Will you text me tomorrow?

defs.text: A noun used in English.
defs.example: This is an example with text message.

defs.text: If something happens literally, it happens exactly as it was said.
defs.example: When I found out that the company would hire me, I literally jumped for joy. In fact, I hit my head on the ceiling.

defs.text: If you remove something, you take it out or away.
defs.example: After he was shot, the doctor removed three bullets from his leg.

defs.text: A performance is a show of acting or music.
defs.example: We went to see a performance by local musicians last night.

defs.text: The performance of a person, machine, company, etc. is how well it does its job.
defs.example: After a year of losing money, the company needs to improve performance.

defs.text: Speed. A rate is how fast something happens. Something can go at a fast rate or a slow rate.
defs.example: The rate of water pouring out of the lake into the river is enough to make the lake empty in a year if it doesn't rain.

defs.text: Someone rates something when they decide how much its value is (how much it's worth).
defs.example: I rate this book at six out of ten: it was not the best book.

defs.text: If something is deeply rooted, felt, held, etc., it is done to a deep extent or degree.
defs.example: I am deeply concerned about this matter.

defs.text: If something moves deeply it moves to or at depth.
defs.example: In this part of the river salmon swim deeply.

defs.text: A scream is a loud noise made by a person.
defs.example: A scream echoed out in the night.

defs.text: If you scream, you yell or shout loudly.
defs.example: I can hear you. You don't need to scream.

defs.text: If you scream, you move quickly; you race.
defs.example: Police cars screamed down the street.

defs.text: arid land with little or no vegetation
To leave, abandon or forsake someone or something.
defs.example: When he left without us, we felt deserted.

defs.text: A vehicle is something that moves people or things from one place to another, for example: cars, planes, boats, etc.
defs.example: Bicycles and wheelchairs are allowed. All other vehicles must stay off the path.

defs.text: An illegal act or object is one that does not follow the law.
defs.example: This drug is illegal in that country. If you are caught with it, you will be arrested.

defs.text: If something is unbelievable, it cannot be believed; it is not believable.
defs.example: You have an unbelievable number of points!

defs.text: If someone is curious, they ask a lot of questions and want to know new things.
If someone or something is curious, he/she/it is strange or unusual.
Candy is a sweet-tasting food.
defs.example: There is a bowl of candy on the table.

defs.text: Bones are the hard, white things inside your body. They give your body its shape.
defs.example: How many bones did a dinosaur have?

defs.text: The boundary of a surface.
An advantage.
defs.example: His speed gives him an edge.

defs.text: A load is something carried, often something heavy.
defs.example: The truck arrived with a load of dog food.

defs.text: Loads/a load of something is a lot of it.
defs.example: We've had a load of problems ever since we got the new stuff.

defs.text: Your load is how much work you have.
defs.example: We hired another person to spread the load a bit more.

defs.text: Load is the amount electrical power produced.
If you load x on y, you put x on y to be carried. Usually there is a lot of x, and/or it is heavy.
defs.example: We loaded the boxes on the truck and set off for Vancouver.

defs.text: If you load a machine, you put in supplies that the machine uses.
defs.example: He loaded the gun, brought it up, and shot the deer in one continuous motion.

defs.text: A boom is the sound that is made from an explosion.
defs.example: The boom of that volcano hurt my ears.

defs.text: A boom can also be any movable pole; in sailing, it is a pole that comes from the bottom of a sail.
A former x (e.g., president, country, wife) used to be the x but is not anymore.
defs.example: Former president Clinton was giving a speech at the school.

defs.text: The former is the first of two things that have already been talked about.
defs.example: I've taught in high school and university. The former (i.e., high school) is more exciting, but university is less stressful.

defs.text: A holiday is a day when people don't go to work or school, often because there is a religious celebration.
defs.example: In North America, Christmas is the biggest holiday of the year.

defs.text: If you sue someone, you take them to court to make them do something they don't want to do, often to make them pay you money.
defs.example: They successfully sued the company they had worked for, winning a combined award of $275,000.

defs.text: If you arrive somewhere, you come to that place, usually the place that you planned to go to.
defs.example: Is everything ready? I expect the guests to arrive soon.

defs.text: If something arrives somewhere, it comes to that place, usually the place that it was supposed to go to.
defs.example: Five days later a letter arrived by Federal Express.

defs.text: If a time or event arrives, it moves from the future into the present.
defs.example: Finally the day arrived for him to come home.

defs.text: The remains of something are parts of something gone that are still here. This is often used for what is left of dead person whose body was damaged or decayed.
If something is decent, it is good enough.
defs.example: He urged all workers to demand a living wage and decent working conditions.

defs.text: If someone is decent, they are usually honest, kind, and fair.
defs.example: A decent society does not ignore poor people.

defs.text: If someone is decent, they are wearing enough clothes to be seen by other people.
defs.example: Excuse me, may I come in? Are you decent?

defs.text: The tip of something is the farthest point of it.
defs.example: She runs her finger down the bird's back and to the tip of its tail.

defs.text: A tip is words or ideas that help you solve a problem.
defs.example: Police say anonymous tips have led them to more than 20 of the stolen items.

defs.text: A tip is a small amount of money that you give to somebody to thank them for good service.
If something is the tip of the iceberg, it is just a small part of something much bigger.
defs.example: The problems we've seen today are just the tip of the iceberg.

defs.text: If something tips, the top of it moves to one side more than the bottom.
defs.example: The piano tipped over as we were putting it on the truck.

defs.text: If you tip something into something else, you pour it.
defs.example: He tipped the water out of the glass by accident.

defs.text: If you tip somebody, you give them money to thank them for good service.
If you tip somebody off, you tell them about something that's going to happen.
defs.example: The police were tipped off by a phone call.

defs.text: A bride is a wife, the female partner in a marriage. Most used for the period of time around the marriage ceremony.
defs.example: Jill was the bride, and Jack was the bridegroom.

defs.text: A penny is a small coin of little value; 100 pennies (or 100 pence) make a pound, a dollar, a euro, etc.
defs.example: This sweet only costs a penny.

defs.text: A claim is something that you say or write without proof.
defs.example: It is difficult to believe claims that the world is ending.

defs.text: If you have a claim to something, you have the right, to own or do it.
defs.example: The government is disputing their claim to the land.

defs.text: A claim is something that you say you have the right to.
defs.example: They have begun looking for gold on their claim in Western Alberta.

defs.text: If you claim something, you say or write that it is true without proof.
defs.example: It is easy to claim that a god exists, but impossible to prove.

defs.text: If you claim something, you say or write that it belongs to you and often you take it.
defs.example: Once you are over 65, there are a variety of government benefits that you can claim.

defs.text: If something claims a life, it kills people.
defs.example: The disease has claimed seven people in Taipei so far this month.

defs.text: Friendship is being friends with someone.
defs.example: Our friendship began in childhood.

defs.text: A desperate action is one that is dangerous or likely to fail, but one that you take because you have no choice.
defs.example: During the fire, some people tried to break through a wall in a desperate attempt to survive.

defs.text: A desperate situation is a very bad one.
defs.example: Trucks have not been able to reach the village for weeks, and the food situation appears desperate.

defs.text: If someone is desperate, they have a very strong want or need for something.
defs.example: We're desperate for money to help these people.

defs.text: A flower is part of a plant. Flowers are often very pretty. Plants make them so that they can make new seeds.
defs.example: The flower of the plant is starting to wilt.

defs.text: The best something can be.
defs.example: She was in the flower of her life.

defs.text: When something starts to bloom.
defs.example: Cherry blossoms are in flower this week.

defs.text: A plant that has flowers.
defs.example: The rose is my favorite flower.

defs.text: If something is dramatic, it is large and sudden.
defs.example: The increase in foreign students has meant a dramatic change in the number of schools.

defs.text: If something is dramatic, it is connected with acting and theatre.
defs.example: In a highly dramatic speech, he brought everyone to his side.

defs.example: I was freezing because I had forgotten my coat.

defs.text: An emperor is the male leader or monarch of an empire.

defs.text: An incident is an event or occurrence.

defs.text: In law, a sentence is the punishment that a judge gives to a criminal.

defs.example: He was sentenced to 15 years in jail for the murder of his friend.

If you are engaged in something, you are interested in it.
defs.example: Americans are very engaged in this year's elections.

defs.text: If you are engaged in something, you do it.
defs.example: He has recently become actively engaged in trying to find a cure for the disease.

defs.text: If two people are engaged, they have promised to marry each other.
defs.example: They've been dating for two years but just became engaged last week.

defs.text: A spy is a person whose job is to get secret information.
defs.example: James Bond is a famous spy from the books by Ian Fleming.

defs.text: A spy is a person who watches other people secretly.
defs.example: The princess was concerned that a spy with a camera would take photos when she went near the pool.

defs.text: A shadow is the dark area that is made when something blocks light, and that is shaped like the thing blocking the light.
defs.example: I saw your shadow against the wall.

defs.text: The darkness in a shadow.
defs.example: The room filled with shadow as the night came.

defs.text: If you shadow someone, you follow them closely without their knowing it.
defs.example: The detective shadowed the thief.

defs.text: If something is being shadowed, it is being covered in shadow or made dark.
defs.example: The curtains shadowed the room.

defs.text: If you shadow someone, you accompany them when they are working so as to learn about an occupation you intend to take up.
An elevator is a machine that moves people and goods up and down between floors of a building.
defs.example: Take the elevator to floor 13.

defs.text: A grain elevator is a building that is used to store wheat, corn, or other grains.

defs.text: Your attitude is your feelings and opinions, especially when your actions show how you feel.
defs.example: He has a really bad attitude towards work.

defs.text: The attitude of an aircraft is the orientation of it that is relative to the horizon or direction of motion.
If something is negative, it is harmful, sad, or otherwise not good.
defs.example: You can believe or not believe, that there's a positive and negative side to everything.

defs.text: If a word, sentence, answer, etc. is negative, it uses a word like no, not, never, etc.
defs.example: Can't is the negative form of can.

defs.text: If someone is a negative person or has a negative attitude, they mainly think about bad things.
defs.example: Her negative attitudes were the result of a hard life.

defs.text: If a test result is negative, the test did not find what it was testing for.
defs.example: There's nothing to worry about. The HIV test is negative.

defs.text: A screen is a flat surface for showing pictures, text or video.
defs.example: The information appears on the computer screen almost right away.

defs.text: A screen is a flat surface between two areas, often letting something in but keeping something out.
defs.example: The hole in the window screen let the bugs in.

defs.text: If you screen blood, people, information, etc., you find or block unwanted things.
defs.example: They carefully screen the blood for viruses before giving it to hospitals.

defs.text: If you screen a movie, a TV show, etc., you put it on a screen.
defs.example: They screened the new movie for the press last week.

defs.text: If you are bored, you have nothing to do or there is nothing interesting.
defs.example: After ten years at the same job, he had grown bored with work.

defs.text: If two things are similar, they are almost the same, or the same in many, but not all, ways.
defs.example: Canadian English is similar to American English, but there are some small differences in pronunciation, and spelling.

defs.text: If two shapes are similar, they have the same shape, but might be different sizes.
defs.example: These two triangles are similar because they have the same angles, but they are not congruent because one is bigger than the other.

defs.text: An understanding person is able to easily see how someone else feels.
defs.example: Thanks for being so understanding about how emotional and erratic I've been acting lately.

defs.text: A person's understanding of something is what they know or think about it.
defs.example: Science helps us to gain a better understanding of natural processes.

defs.text: An understanding is an agreement between two people.
defs.example: We had an understanding. You should have fulfilled your end of the bargain.

defs.text: Understanding is your ability to understand the feelings of other people.
defs.example: Teachers must listen with kindness and understanding to what the young have to say.

defs.text: A chain is a series of round pieces of material joined together to make a line.
defs.example: He got her a gold chain necklace for her birthday.

defs.text: A series of interconnected things.
defs.example: This led to an unfortunate chain of events.

defs.text: A chain of stores is a group of stores that all have the same name, such as McDonald's restaurants or GAP clothing stores.

defs.text: If you fully understand or do something, you understand or do all of it.
defs.example: I have not yet been able to understand this idea fully.

defs.text: A robin is a type of bird that usually has a red breast. European robins are called Erithacus rubecula whereas American robins are called Turdus migratorius.
If you collect some things, you bring them together as a group.
defs.example: The study collected data from 562 mothers in the hospital.

defs.text: Gorgeous is very beautiful.
defs.example: All my classmates agreed that Bella was absolutely gorgeous.

defs.text: Very enjoyable, pleasant, tasty etc.
defs.example: Israeli hummus is absolutely gorgeous.

defs.text: Passion is a strong feeling or emotion.
defs.example: I have a passion for soap operas!

defs.text: A writer is a person who writes books or other things that people read.
defs.example: She works as a writer for a magazine.

defs.text: An empire is a large country that has taken control of many other countries.
An empire is a country led by an emperor or empress.
An empire is a large amount of property and power that a person might have.
defs.example: No mater how rich he got, he kept trying to build his empire bigger.

defs.text: An international event, situation, idea, etc. includes two or more countries.
defs.example: In soccer news, France beat Japan in international competition.

defs.text: An international student is a student from country A studying in country B.
defs.example: The United States has more international students than any other country.

defs.text: A curse is a wish or hope that something bad will happen to someone or something.
defs.example: The evil queen put a curse on the young girl.

defs.text: A curse is a swear word.
A curse is the cause of a lot of harm or evil; it is something that brings evil or harm.
If someone hires you, they agree to give you a job and pay you money.

Someone's estate is everything they own, or everything they leave when they die.
defs.example: Because he had no family, he left his estate to the church.

defs.text: An estate is a large area of land with a large house on it.
defs.example: On the weekend, we went fishing at her country estate.

defs.text: Real estate is land, and the buildings on the land.
defs.example: Most of the company's money is in real estate.

defs.text: Real estate is the business of buying and selling land, and the buildings on the land.
defs.example: A real estate agent helped us to sell our home.

defs.text: A device is a small machine or tool.
defs.example: She has a device in her kitchen for cutting garlic.

defs.text: A device is a machine or part attached to a computer, such as a keyboard, mouse, printer etc.
defs.example: The mouse is an important device for using the computer.

defs.text: A device is a clever way of doing something.
A device is a logo.
A hug is the action of putting your arms around someone else to show love or friendship.
If you hug somebody, you put your arms around them to show love or friendship.
If two people hug, they put their arms around each other to show love or friendship.
Design is how something looks and works.

defs.text: If you design something, you plan and show how it will look and work.
defs.example: The team was asked to design a new video game controller.

defs.text: Movement is the act of moving, of changing place or position.
defs.example: The European Union allows free movement of people between countries.

defs.text: A movement, is a group of people who are all working for the same idea.
defs.example: The labour movement protects the rights of the workers.

defs.text: A movement is a part in a musical composition such as a sonata or symphony.
defs.example: The first movement of the "Moonlight" Sonata is very famous.

defs.text: Thunder is the sound made by lightning.
defs.example: He heard thunder in the distance.

defs.text: Thunder is a loud sound.
defs.example: The thunder of the train was very loud.

defs.text: An object is a thing that you can touch, but it is not alive.
defs.example: We don't know what killed him, but it was a smooth, heavy object.

defs.text: The object of an action or plan is the goal or the reason for it.
defs.example: The object of soccer is to kick the ball into the other team's net.

defs.text: The object is a type of complement in a verb phrase or preposition phrase with the form of a noun phrase.
defs.example: In the sentence Yoko ate the bread, the bread is the object.

defs.text: If you object to something, you don't agree with it.
defs.example: Most people will object to being asked to work too much.

defs.text: A pen is a writing tool that uses ink.

defs.text: A pen is a small area with a fence around it, usually for animals.
defs.example: The pigs walked slowly around their pen.

defs.text: Politics is the activity of controlling, affecting or studying an organisation, especially a government.

defs.text: Alcohol is the chemical in some drinks that makes you drunk (intoxicated).

defs.example: The scientist used an alcohol to fuel the burner.

defs.text: A climb is an upwards movement, often a slow or difficult one.
defs.example: It isn't far, but it's a steep climb and they were sweating when they reach the top.

defs.text: A climb down is a long slow downwards movement.
If you climb something, you move up or down it.
defs.example: They climbed the stairs to the top of the tower again and went out onto the roof.

defs.text: If you climb into, out of, through something, etc., you move with difficulty, often using your hands and knees.
defs.example: The old man climbed into the back seat of her small car.

defs.text: If prices, profits, temperatures, etc. climb or if a road, a path, or a piece of land climbs, it goes up.
defs.example: This year, gas prices have climbed steadily from a low of 75 cents to a peak of almost $1.30 in August.

defs.text: A conference is a large organised meeting to discuss a particular topic or area.
defs.example: FMBRA will be holding a conference on diet, health, and the food industry on 19 March in Barcelona.

defs.text: A conference is a meeting.
defs.example: Contact the teacher or coach and ask for a private conference without your child's presence.

defs.text: When you provide something, you make it available.
defs.example: The restaurant provided food for the party.

defs.text: When you provide, you give means of support.

defs.text: If you earn something you get it by working or doing something.

defs.text: If you think you have earned something, you think you should have it because of what you have done.
defs.example: After completing that project I thought I had earned some time to rest.

A fashion is a style, often clothing, that is popular at a particular time and place.
defs.example: The fashion was for men to have long hair.

defs.text: A fashion is a way or manner.
defs.example: It's a good idea to pay what you owe in a timely fashion.

defs.text: The fashion business is the business of designing and making clothes.
defs.example: Lagerfeld is the current designer for the Chanel fashion house.

defs.text: An episode is an event or a short period of time that is important or unusual.
defs.example: She remembered an especially strange episode that occurred when she was a teenager.

defs.text: An episode is a part of a dramatic work such as a television or radio program.
defs.example: This television series has 10 episodes and will be shown over the next 10 weeks.

defs.text: A prize is something that you receive for winning or doing well.
defs.example: She was the first African woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize.

defs.text: A prize horse, story, performance, etc. is very good and could win a prize.
defs.example: She caught this year's prize fish late yesterday evening.

defs.text: If something was done previously, it was done before.
defs.example: We discovered a language that was previously unknown.

defs.example: She must give the bank £100 to clear (remove) her debt.

defs.text: If you are in debt, you owe money (normally to a bank).
A wire is a long, thin metal thing, mostly for the purpose of making a connection from electric power to a machine.
defs.example: A person cut the electric wire and all the machines in the building stopped.

defs.text: To join a wire to something.
defs.example: They wired up all the machines in the building.

defs.text: A circle (●) is a round shape.
defs.example: Please put your chairs in a circle.

defs.text: To circle something is to move around it.
defs.example: The earth circles the sun once a year.

defs.text: An approach is a way of doing something.
defs.example: We need children and adults to take a proactive approach to reducing gun violence.

defs.text: An approach is movement towards something.
defs.example: And he made a cautious approach to the boat.

defs.text: An approach is the road or path that leads to a place.
defs.example: There were cameras on all approaches to the house.

defs.text: If you approach something, you move closer to it.
defs.example: We're now approaching the last bus stop. Please move towards the door.

defs.text: If you approach a problem, or a job you try to deal with it.
defs.example: We've got a difficult situation here, and I'm not sure how to approach it.

defs.text: Your stock is the collection of things that you have available, usually to sell.
defs.example: It depend on where the store got its stock from.

defs.text: A stock is a share in a public company.
defs.example: ETFs are mutual funds that trade on stock exchanges, just as stocks do.

defs.text: If something is in stock it is at the store and available for sale.
defs.example: I think we have five more in stock.

defs.text: If something is out of stock it is not at the store and available for sale.
defs.example: I'm sorry, we're all out of stock.

defs.text: If a store stocks a product, it has it available to be sold.
defs.example: They are expensive, and most stores won't stock them.

defs.text: If you stock x with y, you fill x with y.
defs.example: I've stocked the fridge with beer for the party.

defs.text: If you stock up on something, you get more than you use in a short time.
defs.example: Residents there are stocking up on food and water for the winter.

defs.text: A stock market is a place where people trade stocks.
You use percent show the number of parts out of a hundred. The symbol for percent is %.
defs.example: The cost of gas has increased seven percent in the last month.

defs.text: One percent of politicians are (not is) honest.
Twenty percent of the water was (not were) dirty.
You use normally to show what usually happens or what you usually do.
defs.example: Normally, we eat lunch at 12:00.

defs.text: A tail is a long, thin part on the back end of an animal.
defs.example: The dog wags his tail (moves his tail quickly from side to side) when he sees his friend.

defs.text: Someone gets an education if that person learns something or if somebody teaches that person something, usually at school.
defs.example: More and more people are starting work with a university education.

defs.text: A library is a place where books and other media are kept, usually on shelves. Most of the time, people are allowed to borrow these things.
defs.example: I borrowed books at the public library today.

defs.text: A library is a collection of books of other media. A person may call his/her collection of books a library.
defs.example: The university's online classical music library is very large.

defs.text: In computing, a library or standard library (STL) is a collection of code and functions that can be used for software development and to make computer programs.
Rape is when someone has sex with a person who does not want to have sex.
defs.example: 6 years ago my ex-boyfriend raped me, and I had to call the police.

defs.text: Rape is when a man has sexual intercourse with a woman against her will.
If a person rapes someone, he or she makes the other person have involuntary sex with him or her.
A tank is a large, strong container for gas or liquid.
defs.example: The gas stove was connected to a propane tank.

defs.text: A tank is a large metal vehicle with a gun that runs on tracks.
defs.example: They do not have heavy weapons such as tanks and armored vehicles.

defs.text: The tank is a room, usually in a police station, for keeping people locked up.
defs.example: The police threw him in the holding tank with us.

defs.text: To have authority means to have the power to make a decision.
defs.example: This judge has the authority to throw you in jail.

defs.text: If you are an authority on something, many people think you know very, very much about it.
defs.example: The Pope is the highest authority in the Catholic church.
